tasks.short: Check preliminary and final proofs, correct errors and record proof approval.

assumptions: Structured intake is preferred; only residual free text uses a model.
Conflicting instructions remain unresolved until a person clarifies them.
GDPR requires suitable access, retention and processing arrangements for personal data sent to a model.
EU AI Act obligations depend on deployment. National rules determine employee consultation requirements.
Build ranges cover a scoped pilot; consultation or access negotiations may extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Whether requesters can adopt a shared intake form.
Which requirements are mandatory for each publication type.
Who may change scope, deadlines and resource commitments.

new_work: Review extracted requirements and missing-field alerts.
Maintain intake fields and dependency templates.
Evaluate extraction failures after brief formats change.
Maintain access controls and processing arrangements.
tasks.statement: Study layout or other design instructions to determine work to be done and sequence of operations.

tasks.short: Import supplied publication files; obsolete disks and tapes are exceptional archive work.

steps.what: Download the supplied source package from the {EMAIL}.
Store the local source package in the correct project folder in the {DOCS}.
Import stored files into publication design software ({OTHER}).
Check missing images, fonts and import errors in publication design software ({OTHER}).

tasks.design: Replace attachment downloads with project-specific intake folders in the {DOCS}, using required project references and existing access controls. A deterministic connector on the {DATA_PLATFORM} imports supported files into publication design software ({OTHER}), checks file counts and missing dependencies, and sends exceptions through the {WORKFLOW}. Unsupported legacy media remain a separate recovery exception.
tasks.previous_blocker: The literal disk-and-tape task is largely obsolete. Its surviving equivalent persists where attachments, project folders and publication design software ({OTHER}) require separate manual transfers.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared intake, file notifications and scripted imports are established capabilities. AI-assisted coding can make a narrow connector cheaper to build, but cannot recover unreadable media.
tasks.still_hard: Old file formats, missing fonts, unavailable readers and damaged media require specialist recovery. An apparently successful import can still change a layout.
tasks.human_edge: The publisher recognises when imported content is incomplete or visually wrong and decides when archive recovery is worth pursuing.
tasks.altitude: Routine transfers leave the week, while import exceptions remain. Decision rights do not change.

reach.task: Prepare complete source packages for production handoff.
reach.learn: Dependency manifests, font permissions and format compatibility.

reach.task: Identify the authoritative version of supplied publication content.
reach.learn: Version provenance and how to resolve conflicting source files.

evidence.claim: Shared file intake and deterministic imports can replace repeated downloading, copying and opening of supported publication files.
Physical disks and tapes are exceptional archive inputs rather than a typical weekly desktop-publishing workflow today.
The digest provides no documented desktop-publishing file-import case; estimates require local validation.

assumptions: The obsolete task is interpreted through its current equivalent: loading supplied publication files.
The stated historical frequency is not assumed to describe current physical-media use.
Time shares cover a routine digital intake case, excluding archive recovery.
Publication design software ({OTHER}) exposes a supported import command or automation interface.
Incoming files receive existing security checks before import.
The low nearly-all prior is rejected for routine digital transfers because their individual steps are deterministic; physical recovery remains manual.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply where relevant. National consultation rules depend on the rollout; no employee monitoring is proposed.
Build ranges exclude damaged-media recovery and any required formal consultation process.
unknowns: Whether physical disks or tapes are still received.
The actual balance of shared-folder intake, attachments and removable media.
Which file formats and import interfaces are supported.
Whether current import checks detect missing dependencies reliably.
Retention requirements and access restrictions for source packages.
Whether any remaining archive collection needs specialist recovery.
research_questions: Can direct intake remove the attachment-download step for regular contributors?
Which import failures can be detected from manifests and application error reports?
Does a representative file set retain layout fidelity after unattended import?
new_work: Resolve unsupported formats, missing dependencies and failed imports.
Maintain intake permissions, project references and connector compatibility.
Check representative imports after publication design software ({OTHER}) updates.
Arrange specialist recovery when legacy media are actually encountered.
tasks.statement: Load floppy disks or tapes containing information into system.

tasks.short: Convert publication files into print or web formats, check the result, and deliver the correct version.

steps.what: Read destination and delivery requirements in {EMAIL}.
Choose export settings in the {OTHER} conversion application.
Export publication files in the {OTHER} conversion application.
Inspect converted pages and preflight results in the {OTHER} validation application.
Approve delivery and send publication files through {EMAIL}.

tasks.design: A configured intake in {WORKFLOW} selects approved export profiles in the {OTHER} conversion application and stores versioned outputs and preflight reports in {DOCS}. A small integration prepares delivery through {EMAIL} or upload to {CMS}; the desktop publisher checks the output and approves the destination-specific release.
tasks.previous_blocker: Destination requirements, source versions and export settings were disconnected. Unusual fonts, effects and legacy formats made unattended conversion unreliable.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing export presets and preflight tools handle standard formats. Faster coding makes version tracking, delivery preparation and exception routing economical.
tasks.still_hard: Legacy files, missing fonts and flattened content can lose fidelity. Accessible web documents may require manual reading-order and semantic checks.
tasks.human_edge: Notice a technically valid conversion that changes meaning, readability or visual emphasis.

ambition.what: Versioned print-and-web release pack with a linked preflight report

tasks.altitude: Routine export setup and file delivery occupy less of the week. The desktop publisher can offer a traceable release pack; publication approval rights stay unchanged.

reach.task: Specify publication assets for accessible, responsive web use.
reach.learn: Web image formats, compression, document accessibility and responsive asset requirements.

evidence.claim: CHILI GraFx fills governed layout templates, supporting repeatable publication generation.
The template evidence does not establish reliable conversion of arbitrary legacy files.
Export profiles and preflight checks can automate standard conversions, with human review for fidelity and accessibility.
The time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates.

assumptions: The {OTHER} conversion application supports reusable profiles and batch export.
Print requirements apply to print outputs; web requirements apply to web outputs.
Future routine requests use structured destination fields instead of free-text email instructions.
File delivery and upload are gated; direct website publication requires the existing publication approval.
Access estimates include assessing consultation under national rules; required consultation may extend the range.
GDPR applies to personal data in source and output files. Any introduced model use also needs assessment under the EU AI Act.
unknowns: Which source and destination formats account for most jobs?
Can the installed conversion tools run unattended under current licences?
What accessibility requirements apply to the outputs?
Does delivery mean printer handoff, draft upload or direct publication?
Who may approve each destination and release?
research_questions: Which format pairs preserve fonts, transparency, links and reading order reliably?
Which preflight checks and visual comparisons expose meaningful conversion failures?
How should retries prevent duplicate delivery or release of an outdated version?
new_work: Maintain destination profiles and regression samples.
Resolve missing fonts and unsupported source formats.
Review flagged visual changes and accessibility issues.
Approve releases and investigate failed deliveries.
Maintain version links and destination credentials.
tasks.statement: Convert various types of files for printing or for the Internet, using computer software.

tasks.short: Enter image positions and colour settings, retouch images, and check publication proofs.

steps.what: Read correction specifications and locate source images in {DOCS}.
Enter coordinates, colour values and profiles in {OTHER} image-editing software.
Retouch selected areas in {OTHER} image-editing software using visual judgement.
Compare the proof against specifications and approve image corrections.

tasks.design: A small rules-based importer reads structured correction specifications from {DOCS} and supplies saved actions in {OTHER} image-editing software. It preserves originals and produces comparison proofs; the desktop publisher handles local retouching and approves visual quality before corrected images enter the publication.
tasks.previous_blocker: Correction specifications and image settings were separate, while short production runs made custom import scripts difficult to justify.
tasks.enabler_now: Saved actions, colour profiles and scripting already handle repeatable edits. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of connecting them to a consistent specification format.
tasks.still_hard: Mixed lighting, skin tones, selective masks and differences between screen and printed output still require visual judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising when a technically valid correction makes an image less credible or weakens the intended message.

ambition.what: Choose between print colour treatments for campaign variants before final proof approval.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from entering settings to comparing proofs and resolving difficult images. The publisher can select treatments within approved colour standards; changes to those standards still need the design lead.

reach.task: Prepare reusable image treatment specifications.
reach.learn: Colour management, mask design and how image treatments support the visual hierarchy.

evidence.claim: Saved actions and colour profiles can apply repeatable numeric corrections; visual retouching remains less predictable.
The proposed effort and remaining-time figures are planning estimates, not measured results.

assumptions: This describes recurring publication work in a mid-size European marketing team.
Most correction specifications contain explicit coordinates, colour values or approved presets.
The {OTHER} image-editing software supports saved actions; available scripting determines the importer scope.
Estimates cover a limited image workflow, not replacement of the creative toolset.
Access work includes checking GDPR requirements where images identify people; consultation follows national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Which correction specifications are numeric and which require interpretation?
Which scripting interfaces and licensed features are available in {OTHER}?
Who may approve colour changes and which output profiles must be used?
Do image rights or personal data restrict processing?
Does the proposed implementation require employee consultation under national rules?
research_questions: Can saved actions reproduce approved corrections across representative image formats?
Which proof comparisons reveal print defects that automated file checks miss?
new_work: Maintain preset versions and specification field mappings.
Review failed imports, unsupported profiles and unexpected image dimensions.
Check comparison proofs and test presets after software or printer-profile changes.
tasks.statement: Enter data, such as coordinates of images and color specifications, into system to retouch and make color corrections.

tasks.short: Choose publication colours, produce separations, and check that they meet the print specification.

steps.what: Read the publication brief and printer specification in {EMAIL}.
Inspect artwork inks and colour spaces in the {OTHER} prepress application.
Choose process and spot colours in the {OTHER} prepress application.
Generate separation files using the {OTHER} prepress application.
Review separation proofs in {DOCS} and approve the files.

tasks.design: Configure printer presets and separation checks in the {OTHER} prepress application, using approved specifications held in {DOCS}. A configured intake in {WORKFLOW} supplies print requirements; the desktop publisher chooses the colour plan and approves separation proofs before downstream release.
tasks.previous_blocker: Printer specifications arrived separately from artwork. Presets varied, and colour choices involved brand appearance, substrate and print cost.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing prepress controls already handle ink inventories and separations. Faster implementation makes specification intake, preset maintenance and linked proofs cheaper to connect.
tasks.still_hard: Screens cannot fully predict ink on a particular substrate. Special finishes, overprints and unusual spot colours still need experienced judgement or a physical proof.
tasks.human_edge: Judge whether the printed result preserves the intended appearance within the available budget.

ambition.what: Per-edition comparison of process-only and spot-colour options

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from repeated separation setup toward evaluating difficult colour choices. Existing colour approval and spending authority stay unchanged.

reach.task: Prepare artwork that reproduces consistently across print substrates.
reach.learn: Colour management, ink limits, overprint behaviour and physical proof evaluation.

evidence.claim: Prepress applications commonly provide ink inventories, separation previews and reusable output presets.
Substrate effects and special inks can require physical proofs despite automated technical checks.
The time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured case results.

assumptions: Most jobs use an established printer and known print specifications.
Structured intake replaces routine reading of specification emails; unusual requirements enter an exception queue.
The {OTHER} prepress application supports presets and separation inspection.
Access estimates include assessing employee consultation under national rules; required consultation may extend the range.
GDPR applies where artwork contains personal data. Applicable EU AI Act obligations must be assessed if model features are introduced.
unknowns: Which prepress application and automation interfaces are available?
How many jobs use special inks, finishes or unfamiliar substrates?
Who approves colour choices and additional print spending?
Are printer specifications current and reusable?
Which national consultation requirements apply to this workplace?
research_questions: Which configured checks detect unintended spot inks and overprints in the supported file formats?
Which proofing method provides sufficient confidence for each substrate and finish?
new_work: Maintain printer presets and specification versions.
Investigate unexpected inks and failed separation checks.
Review generated proofs and request physical proofs where needed.
Revalidate presets when a printer changes its process.
tasks.statement: Select number of colors and determine color separations.

tasks.short: Prepare an approved publication master, send it to the printer, and confirm receipt.

steps.what: Collect printer specifications, delivery details and the approved master from {EMAIL} and {DOCS}.
Export and preflight the master in {OTHER} publication software against printer requirements.
Check the release and send the production package through {PARTNER_PORTAL}.
Check the printer acknowledgement in {EMAIL} and record receipt in {PROJECT}.

tasks.design: Configured export and preflight profiles in {OTHER} publication software prepare a production package from the approved master in {DOCS}. A flow in {WORKFLOW} presents the exact file, destination and print order for release approval, then submits through {PARTNER_PORTAL} and records acknowledgement in {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Printer requirements, file versions and acknowledgements sat in separate places. Different submission methods made a single reliable handoff difficult.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing export profiles and workflow approvals cover much of the task. A small connector can bind the approved file version to its destination and delivery receipt.
tasks.still_hard: Some printers lack supported upload interfaces. Special finishes, unusual page construction and production changes require direct discussion with the printer.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding whether a production exception is acceptable before a release creates printing costs.
tasks.altitude: The publisher spends less time assembling uploads and chasing receipts, and more time resolving preflight exceptions. Release authority stays the same; no new spending rights are gained.

reach.task: Specify artwork for special print finishes.
reach.learn: Printer tolerances, finishing constraints and how production choices affect artwork.

evidence.claim: Configured export profiles, preflight rules and approval workflows can automate routine preparation and delivery checks.
The digest contains no documented printer-handoff case supporting a measured time-saving claim.

assumptions: Digital delivery through {PARTNER_PORTAL} is the usual route; film and plate production are handled by the printer.
The print order already has budget approval; this task authorises release of the production file.
The publisher has delegated release authority within the approved print order.
The connector uses a supported submission interface and structured receipts.
Estimates cover one printer route. Access includes external credentials and GDPR checks for any personal data sent; consultation follows national rules where applicable.

Does a retry risk creating a duplicate production job?
Which print requirements can be checked before submission?
new_work: Maintain printer specifications, destinations and export profiles.
Resolve rejected files, missing receipts and uncertain submission outcomes.
Review the release package before sending and test duplicate prevention after connector changes.
tasks.statement: Transmit, deliver, or mail publication master to printer for production into film and plates.

tasks.short: Coordinate contributors and assemble publication masters that meet design specifications.

steps.what: Gather copy, artwork and revision comments from {DOCS} and {EMAIL}.

loop.input: Revision comments linked to named files, pages and contributors.
loop.output: A draft revision register with source references, conflicts and unanswered questions.
loop.check: Require a source reference for every entry; validate file identifiers and let the publisher confirm conflicts.
loop.stop: One extraction pass and one correction pass per revision batch; unresolved entries go to the publisher.
loop.why_not_simpler: File collection is deterministic, but free-text comments express changes and contradictions inconsistently.

steps.what: Resolve conflicting edits and design trade-offs with writers and designers.
Assemble copy and artwork in {OTHER} publication software using agreed revisions.
Review the proof with contributors and approve content and layout.
Freeze the approved master and record its version in {DOCS}.

tasks.design: A shared revision register in {WORKFLOW} links comments to source versions in {DOCS}; a bounded extraction loop drafts entries from free-text feedback. Governed templates in {OTHER} publication software assemble recurring layouts, while contributors resolve disagreements and the editor approves the proof. The recorded approval freezes the corresponding master in {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Version confusion and scattered comments consumed coordination time. Layout automation needed maintained templates, while unusual pages still required skilled composition.
tasks.enabler_now: Governed layout templates are available today, and a bounded reading loop can organise comments without deciding editorial conflicts. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of connecting the revision register, files and approval records.
tasks.still_hard: Persuading contributors to settle conflicting priorities remains human work. New formats, complex tables and substantial text changes can exceed template limits.
tasks.human_edge: Negotiating meaning, visual emphasis and editorial compromises when several valid choices conflict.

ambition.what: An early multilingual layout feasibility check before copy is finalised.

tasks.altitude: The publisher spends more time anticipating layout problems and discussing alternatives with contributors. They can propose format and length changes earlier; editorial approval remains with the editor.

reach.task: Set copy-length budgets before commissioning publication sections.
reach.learn: Editorial structure, audience priorities and how to negotiate cuts without losing meaning.

reach.task: Assess layout constraints for translated editions.
reach.learn: Text expansion, script requirements and language-specific reading order.

evidence.claim: CHILI GraFx fills governed layout templates, supporting the proposed template assembly component.
Source-linked extraction can help organise revision comments, but the digest provides no measured case for this collaboration workflow.

assumptions: Recurring publication families account for enough work to justify maintained templates.
Contributors use a mixture of documents, messages and review conversations.
The first rollout covers one publication family and one revision intake route.
The loop drafts revision entries and does not autonomously rewrite approved copy.
GDPR applies to contributor data; EU AI Act duties must be assessed for the chosen use and deployment.
Access estimates include a bounded employee consultation allowance where national rules require it; procurement delays are excluded.

Where do authoritative copy, artwork and comments currently live?

Which languages and accessibility requirements must templates support?
May revision comments be processed by the selected model service?
Which consultation and access approvals are required?

Which recurring layouts can templates reproduce without frequent manual repair?
How should late comments reopen an approved version without losing its audit trail?
new_work: Review extracted revisions, especially ambiguous instructions and conflicts.
Maintain templates, field constraints and overflow checks.
Test the extraction prompt against representative comments after changes.
Resolve version mismatches and maintain contributor permissions.
tasks.statement: Collaborate with graphic artists, editors and writers to produce master copies according to design specifications.

tasks.short: Create image effects, sound and animation for electronic publications, then prepare approved files for publication.

steps.what: Read the publication brief and clarify intended effects with the marketing manager.
Collect images, audio and usage permissions from the {DOCS}.
Choose composition, effects and pacing in publication design software ({OTHER}).
Build vignettes, mosaics and image composites in publication design software ({OTHER}).
Add sound, animation and playback controls in publication design software ({OTHER}).
Preview playback and correct visual, audio and accessibility faults in publication design software ({OTHER}).
Review the publication proof and approve it or request changes through the {EMAIL}.
Export approved files from publication design software ({OTHER}) to the {DOCS}.

tasks.design: Configure reusable effect presets, motion templates and export profiles in publication design software ({OTHER}); a portable specification defines required assets and outputs. A small job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} assembles assets from the {DOCS}, checks technical constraints and returns exceptions to the desktop publisher. The {WORKFLOW} records approval of a specific proof version before its publication package reaches the {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Custom composition and pacing resist fixed rules. Reusable presets already existed, but inconsistent asset names, permissions and output requirements limited their reuse.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing presets cover repeated effects. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of building asset manifests, technical checks and approval connections; no visual judgement breakthrough is assumed.
tasks.still_hard: Original compositions, awkward image crops, audio balance and playback across devices still require skilled attention. File metadata cannot establish every usage right.
tasks.human_edge: The publisher decides what draws attention, how motion supports meaning and when an effect distracts or excludes the audience.
tasks.altitude: The week contains fewer repeated transformations and exports, with more time for composition and playback testing. The publisher can recommend motion treatments and accessible alternatives; campaign approval remains with the marketing manager.

reach.task: Develop reusable campaign compositions.
reach.learn: Visual hierarchy, crop rules and how to preserve a concept across formats.

reach.task: Specify accessible motion and playback behaviour.
reach.learn: Reduced-motion preferences, keyboard controls and device testing.

evidence.claim: Governed layout templates can generate publication variants; this supports template filling, not arbitrary multimedia composition.
Effect presets, export profiles and deterministic technical checks can reduce repeated production work while leaving creative choices human.
The proposed remaining-time percentages and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured results.

assumptions: The steps represent a mixed queue of original publications and repeat campaign variants.
Time shares describe a typical production pass; rejected proofs repeat the relevant production steps.
Publication design software ({OTHER}) supports reusable presets and export profiles.
The low model-needed prior is retained: no model loop is needed for this design.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply where relevant. National rules may require employee consultation if the rollout changes working arrangements or introduces monitoring.
Consent and access estimates cover ordinary permissions and consultation screening; any required formal consultation may extend elapsed time.
unknowns: The proportion of original compositions versus repeated variants.
Available automation interfaces in publication design software ({OTHER}).
Whether asset permissions are recorded in usable fields.
Required output formats, devices and accessibility standards.
Who currently approves proofs and whether approval is version-specific.
Whether personal data or employee monitoring enters the proposed workflow.

Which technical faults can be detected reliably before visual review?
How much review time remains when presets are tested on representative publications?
new_work: Maintain presets, motion templates and export profiles.
Review asset matches and unresolved usage permissions.
Investigate technical check failures and playback differences.
Keep proof approvals tied to the exact exported version.
Test reduced-motion editions and maintain their acceptance criteria.
tasks.statement: Create special effects such as vignettes, mosaics, and image combining, and add elements such as sound and animation to electronic publications.

role_batches.altitude: The publisher spends less time assembling files, repeating formatting and reconciling comments. More time goes to visual hierarchy, difficult production cases and editorial coordination; final publication authority changes only through explicit organisational delegation.
reach: Help event planners produce dependable programmes from approved schedules.
Work with editors on terminology and evidence-backed corrections.
Help web and digital interface designers preserve reading order across formats.
Give marketing managers clearer production consequences for late changes.
skills_to_grow: Content schemas, asset metadata and version control.
Print preflight and accessible document structure.
Evaluation of model-proposed corrections against source evidence.
role_batches.ambitious_version: Offer a governed publication service that lets adjacent teams prepare routine materials from approved content, while the publisher concentrates on composition, exceptions and production quality.

role_batches.altitude: The role moves from repeated file assembly toward publication quality, accessibility and production advice. The publisher gains bounded decisions over typography, sample shortlists and asset readiness; marketing approval remains with the marketing manager.
reach: Graphic designer: develop and explain visual directions.
Proofreader: verify meaning and reading order after layout changes.
Marketing manager: assess publication feasibility while briefs are being shaped.
role_batches.ambitious_version: Provide a publication readiness service that checks briefs and assets early, offers audience-specific layout directions and supports large-print editions.

role_batches.altitude: The week shifts toward visual quality, difficult source material and release readiness as repeated intake, setup and export work shrinks. The role can coordinate a traceable publication pack, while existing creative, budget and publication approval rights remain in place.
reach: Graphic design: prepare consistent colour reproduction, image treatments and campaign crops.
Web and digital interface design: specify usable publication assets and check accessible outputs.
Technical writing: improve source structure, table semantics and asset traceability.
skills_to_grow: Prepress presets, colour management and proof evaluation.
Structured content intake and asset metadata.
Export automation, preflight checks and version control.
Source-linked OCR review and exception handling.
Image comparison, reversible editing and model evaluation.
Accessible document and web asset preparation.
role_batches.ambitious_version: Provide a publication readiness service that turns approved source packs into traceable print and web outputs, with clear technical checks and targeted human visual approval.

role_batches.altitude: The desktop publisher becomes a publication production specialist who spends more time on visual quality, layout feasibility and production exceptions. They gain room to propose treatments and reusable formats; editorial, spending and records-policy authority change only through explicit delegation.
reach: Help graphic designers turn recurring treatments into usable production specifications.
Help editors set copy-length budgets before layout begins.
Help translators identify layout constraints before translated editions are assembled.
Help event planners find and reuse approved publication material.
skills_to_grow: Template design, structured content and overflow handling.
Source-linked revision review and editorial negotiation.
Archive metadata, permissions and recovery verification.
role_batches.ambitious_version: Offer an early production-readiness service that checks layout, language expansion, image treatment and print constraints before publication commitments are fixed.

role_batches.altitude: The desktop publisher spends less time transferring files and repeating effects, and more time shaping composition and checking audience experience. They gain scope to propose accessible publication variants; final campaign approval stays with the marketing manager.
reach: Graphic designers: turn approved visual concepts into reusable production templates.
Web and digital interface designers: specify motion, controls and accessible playback.
Editors: establish source provenance and complete production handoffs.
role_batches.ambitious_version: Offer a repeatable service that produces standard and reduced-motion campaign editions from the same approved assets, with human control over composition and pacing.
